B1J2RMorJXM.summary: Robert Wills of TNMoC explains the Apollo Guidance Computer hardware and software, then walks through the Apollo 11 landing procedure step by step, including the 1202 alarms.
B1J2RMorJXM.why: HN calls it mandatory viewing on the AGC, praising the speaker's enthusiasm and the clear account of restartable, robust software design.

BLGFriOKz6U.summary: Apple security head Ivan Krstic gives a Black Hat 2016 talk on iOS security, covering HomeKit, Auto Unlock and iCloud Keychain. He explains key hierarchies and how data can stay safe even in adversarial clouds.
BLGFriOKz6U.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the deepest public look at how iCloud Keychain and Apple's device and cloud security are designed.

BzhbAK1pdPM.summary: The first clip from Russell Barkley's 30 Essential Ideas about ADHD series, introducing ADHD as a chronic developmental disability. It is part of a lecture series on the disorder by a leading ADHD researcher.
BzhbAK1pdPM.why: HN commenters repeatedly recommend Barkley's lectures as the best introduction to understanding ADHD.

BFld4EBO2RE.summary: Inigo Quilez live-paints a mountain landscape using only math in a shader, building up from a basic polynomial noise surface through fractal terrain, lighting and atmosphere. The code runs in real time on Shadertoy so viewers can edit it as they follow along.
BFld4EBO2RE.why: HN commenters point to it as the best demonstration of procedural graphics from a master, accessible to beginners yet deep enough for advanced viewers.

BzB5xtGGsTc.summary: Wendover Productions explains how airlines make money from different cabin classes and why premium seats matter so much to profits. It also touches on how this shaped decisions such as the decline of supersonic travel.
BzB5xtGGsTc.why: HN commenters recommend it as an in-depth, accessible look at airline class economics and revisit it in many discussions about airlines.

BCmz-fgp24E.summary: Oh The Urbanity! argues that most city dwellers live in dense residential neighbourhoods outside downtown, which can be calm and peaceful. It draws on older, denser parts of Toronto and Montreal.
BCmz-fgp24E.why: HN users repeatedly post it to rebut the idea that urban living means Manhattan or Hong Kong apartment blocks.

Bd8_vO5zrjo.summary: Part one of Montemayor's animated-map documentary on the Battle of Midway, told using only the information available to the Japanese side. It focuses on Nagumo's dilemma.
Bd8_vO5zrjo.why: HN recommends it for its information-dense maps and voice-over and for showing how commanders decide with limited information.

BxQw4CdxLr8.summary: Donald Knuth's 2017 Christmas Tree Lecture at Stanford about a combinatorial geometry problem whose computed numbers matched a striking formula. He tells the story of the conjecture and its sequel.
BxQw4CdxLr8.why: HN fans love it for Knuth's humor and for how he makes open math problems feel approachable, and it is often cited for details like dancing links and counting rectangle subdivisions.

BickMFHAZR0.summary: Veritasium explains how trees lift water from roots to the top of tall trunks, using transpiration pull and the negative pressure that liquid water can sustain. It explains why trees do not need pumps or valves.
BickMFHAZR0.why: HN commenters recommend it as one of Veritasium's best videos and one that has aged well.

BYRTvoZ3Rho.summary: Numberphile interviews cryptographer Ron Rivest about end-to-end verifiable voting. He explains how homomorphic encryption and receipts let a voter confirm their ballot was counted without being able to prove how they voted to anyone else.
BYRTvoZ3Rho.why: HN commenters point to it in election-security threads as an accessible explainer of how a vote can be verifiable but not sellable.

Bv_5Zv5c-Ts.summary: The first 3.5 hours of Tony Alicea's Udemy course on JavaScript's inner workings, covering topics such as first-class functions, closures, prototypal inheritance and how the language behaves under the hood.
Bv_5Zv5c-Ts.why: HN commenters call it one of the best JavaScript courses: rigorous and deep but not boring, and freely available.

B5NULPSiOGw.summary: Martin Kleppmann's QCon London 2018 talk on keeping data consistent in distributed systems without a central leader. It surveys CRDT algorithms for syncing devices and collaborative editing over peer-to-peer networks.
B5NULPSiOGw.why: Strongly recommended as a clear, accessible survey of the CRDT landscape.

B965f8AcNbw.summary: An episode of Fall of Civilizations on the Late Bronze Age Collapse around 1100 BC, when many Eastern Mediterranean societies were destroyed in a short span. It explores the Sea Peoples and the lessons for modern globalised societies.
B965f8AcNbw.why: HN commenters recommend it as an engaging, high-quality introduction to the Bronze Age Collapse and praise the channel generally.

Bkm2Vfj42FY.summary: Mark Blyth's 2016 Brown University lecture on global Trumpism, explaining the rise of populism through economics, the decline of Western middle classes and revolt against technocracy.
Bkm2Vfj42FY.why: HN recommends it as a concise, chart-backed explanation of the economics behind anti-establishment politics.

B2482h_TNwg.summary: Branch Education's animated deep dive into ASML's EUV photolithography machine and how it prints nanometer-scale transistors onto chips. It covers the system's components and the process of chip manufacturing.
B2482h_TNwg.why: HN sends people here as the most straightforward and detailed starting point for understanding EUV lithography.

B8Y146v8HxE.summary: The first episode of Clickspring's series building a John Wilding skeleton clock from raw stock in a home machine shop. It covers making the frames along with the tools needed for the job.
B8Y146v8HxE.why: Recommended as an absorbing masterpiece of craftsmanship, often raised in threads about watches and clockmaking.

BEG-ly9tQGk.summary: Archer Lars Andersen demonstrates fast, accurate shooting techniques he says he revived from historical art and texts, arguing Hollywood archery is not historical.
BEG-ly9tQGk.why: Recommended as an entertaining example of rediscovered lost skills, though some commenters note it is contested.

ByNs9TG30E8.summary: David Nolen presents Om Next, the redesign of the ClojureScript Om library, drawing on Relay, Netflix's JSONGraph and Datomic. He covers the tradeoffs in handling the client-server boundary over immutable data.
ByNs9TG30E8.why: HN commenters recommend it as the lead ClojureScript developer's own account of Om's evolution, one-way data flow and single-state design.

BDqvzFY72mg.summary: The opening lecture of Ian Shapiro's Yale course Power and Politics in Today's World, which examines political dynamics and institutions over the past quarter century, including inequality, declining unions and new forms of authoritarianism.
BDqvzFY72mg.why: HN recommends the lecture series as a foundational, wide-ranging grounding in modern global politics.

B_nGEj8wIP0.summary: An 86-minute Milton Friedman talk arguing that inflation is a monetary phenomenon caused by money supply growing faster than goods, and that the cure is less government spending and money printing.
B_nGEj8wIP0.why: Shared during inflation discussions as an accessible, layman-friendly statement of the monetarist view.

Bqx6li5dbEY.summary: A short excerpt from Werner Herzog's film Lo and Behold in which Ted Nelson lays out his ideas about hypertext and interconnection. Herzog concludes that Nelson is the only sane person in computing.
Bqx6li5dbEY.why: HN shares it as an accessible window into Ted Nelson's vision of Xanadu and linking, which commenters say gains meaning with historical context.

BrK7X_XlGB8.summary: Julia Galef uses pictures to explain Bayes' rule, then tells three personal stories showing how she applies it to improve her thinking.
BrK7X_XlGB8.why: HN recommends it as a short, accessible intro to Bayesian reasoning and priors.

BCiZc0n6COY.summary: The first lecture of David MacKay's Cambridge course on information theory, pattern recognition and neural networks. It introduces the core ideas of his book Information Theory, Inference, and Learning Algorithms.
BCiZc0n6COY.why: Recommended as an enjoyable, clear introduction to information theory that pairs well with MacKay's free textbook.

BKP1I7IocYU.summary: Folding Ideas' long essay on why playing poorly in World of Warcraft feels rude. It traces how raiding culture shifted from relaxed fun to optimization, theorycrafting and wikis.
BKP1I7IocYU.why: Recommended as a thoughtful, research-heavy dive into game culture and the social pressure of competitive play.

BTHvs3V8DBA.summary: A Google Tech Talk on Yahoo's 14 rules for faster web pages and the YSlow tool. It covers front-end practices like avoiding @import and fixing ETags, with live analysis of popular sites.
BTHvs3V8DBA.why: Praised as solid, research-backed advice on front-end web performance.

BTlUyS-T-_4.summary: Gary's Economics argues that the UK housing crisis stems from wealth inequality, treating housing as an asset like shares that rich people bid up. He contends that simply building more housing won't fix affordability.
BTlUyS-T-_4.why: HN commenters share it as a counterargument to the YIMBY build-more-housing view, linking wealth concentration to asset prices.

BXmOlCy0oBM.summary: A 12-minute film in which Erlang's creators demonstrate the language's fault tolerance and live-system features, including phoning each other to show it working. This version has fixed audio.
BXmOlCy0oBM.why: HN recommends it as a charming, concise demonstration of what makes Erlang special, from the people who built it.

Bca5_uyH9E4.summary: Sam Holmes Sailing visits sailing legend Sven Yrvind and tours his boat, covering the man and his small-boat design philosophy.
Bca5_uyH9E4.why: HN recommends it as an accessible introduction to Yrvind and his minimalist boat ideas.

Bd2bbHoVQSM.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on timeshares covers how people get sold into them, why they are so hard to leave, and the exit-company scams that target owners trying to get out.
Bd2bbHoVQSM.why: Cited in threads about hard-to-cancel subscriptions and timeshare scams as an informative overview of the sketchy exit industry.

Bea4FS-zDzc.summary: SuperfastMatt looks at how the Tesla Model S retracting door handles were redesigned over time, from many parts to a motor plus sensor, with a focus on engineering and reliability.
Bea4FS-zDzc.why: Recommended whenever door handles or car reliability engineering come up, as an enjoyable look at design iteration.

BiKfWdXXfIs.summary: A 2015 interview in which physicist Freeman Dyson, then 91, argues that global warming concerns are exaggerated, that CO2 is beneficial and that climate models oversimplify complex systems. It is posted on a channel that opposes climate consensus.
BiKfWdXXfIs.why: HN commenters point to it as a prominent physicist's skeptical counter-view, usually when someone asks for dissenting opinions.

BiqDZlAZygU.summary: Rowan Atkinson's speech at the launch of the Reform Section 5 campaign in Parliament in 2012. He argues against criminalizing insulting words and for answering speech with more speech.
BiqDZlAZygU.why: Recommended as an eloquent defense of free speech against laws on offensive or insulting speech.

BwGsr3SzCZc.summary: Journalist Matthew Cole's Black Hat 2013 talk on the CIA's operational security failures in the 2003 Milan kidnapping. Phone and location metadata exposed the team and led to arrest warrants.
BwGsr3SzCZc.why: Recommended as a non-technical, concrete case study of how metadata and phone records expose covert operations.

B5FxFfymI4g.summary: Clayton Christensen explains disruptive innovation using the steel industry, showing how mini-mills beat incumbents from the low end. He argues disruption is not about stupid or bad management.
B5FxFfymI4g.why: HN recommends it as an amazing, clear explanation of why incumbents move upmarket and lose to low-end challengers.

B8ofWFx525s.summary: Eli Pariser's TED talk argues that personalized web services trap users in filter bubbles, limiting exposure to challenging information. He says this is bad for individuals and for democracy.
B8ofWFx525s.why: Cited as an early, prescient warning about algorithmic personalization, echo chambers and social media feeds.

B9ly7JjqEb0.summary: Not Just Bikes looks at the tiny microcars such as the Canta seen around Amsterdam. It discusses how they serve people with mobility issues, can use bike paths under certain rules, and where they fit in a 21st century city.
B9ly7JjqEb0.why: Linked in self-driving and car-dependence threads as an example of small vehicles that help disabled and elderly people without full-size cars.

BBwepkVurCI.summary: A clip from Charlie Brooker's BBC show Screenwipe showing how reality TV uses editing to manufacture emotion and narrative. It demonstrates how the same footage can be cut to give very different impressions.
BBwepkVurCI.why: HN people cite it as a vivid demonstration of how editing shapes perception in documentaries and reality television.

BD6h-wDj7bw.summary: Veritasium explains X-chromosome inactivation, where different cells in a woman's body switch off different X chromosomes, giving a mosaic pattern. It uses animation from the WEHI institute and connects to calico cat coloring.
BD6h-wDj7bw.why: Commenters point to it as the best short explanation of X inactivation and why calico cats and some human traits are mosaics.

BHIo6qwJarI.summary: Music video for Public Service Broadcasting's "Go!" from the album The Race For Space, built from NASA audio and archival material of Apollo-era voices.
BHIo6qwJarI.why: HN recommends it as an energizing space-themed song, and references it when Apollo go/no-go calls come up.

BdHK_r9RXTc.summary: Reggie Watts performs at TED 2012, blending vocal looping, beatboxing, poetry and comedy across musical genres in a larger-than-life improvised set.
BdHK_r9RXTc.why: HN points to it as a memorable performance that doubles as a parody of TED talks and a showcase of live vocal looping.

BnSUk0je6oo.summary: John Carmack's keynote at Facebook Connect 2021, where he speaks candidly about VR, Quest, and Meta's metaverse plans. He pushes back on hype and discusses retention and latency.
BnSUk0je6oo.why: Commenters praise it as clear, honest thinking from Carmack and recommend it to technical people interested in VR and the metaverse.

B90_SNNbcoU.summary: Louis Rossmann examines fuses sold on Amazon that fail to trip at their rated current, including a 2A fuse surviving 8 amps. He uses it to criticize Amazon's lax control over safety-relevant products.
B90_SNNbcoU.why: HN cites it as the key example of Amazon selling dangerous counterfeit goods and warns people to test their fuses.

BBJTeNTZtGU.summary: A School of Life short introducing Michel Foucault, who questioned assumed progress in how society treats madness, medicine and sexuality.
BBJTeNTZtGU.why: HN recommends it as a simple entry point to Foucault, especially on mental health and institutionalization.

BHEbVh3Yhrw.summary: Louis Rossmann interviews Kaylie Milliken and Mellissa Wood, producers of the documentary Billion Dollar Bully, about Yelp's alleged practices toward businesses.
BHEbVh3Yhrw.why: Recommended as a good conversation and starting point on Yelp's alleged bullying of businesses.

BI-old7YI4I.summary: Isaac Arthur examines options for colonizing Venus, from vast floating habitats in the temperate upper atmosphere to full terraforming of the planet. It is a long-form speculative futurism episode in his solar system colonization series.
BI-old7YI4I.why: HN commenters cite it as the go-to reference for the idea of living in Venus's atmosphere rather than on the surface.

BpsMkLaEiOY.summary: Brad Fitzpatrick records himself struggling to silence a set of first-generation Nest Protect smoke alarms that keep beeping and triggering one another.
BpsMkLaEiOY.why: HN cites it as the famous example of how over-clever smart-home devices can fail at something as basic as a smoke alarm.

BsVydyC8ZGQ.summary: The official demo video from Be, Inc. showing BeOS running multiple videos, media applications and a responsive desktop on 1990s hardware.
BsVydyC8ZGQ.why: HN people cite it as evidence of how fast and responsive a well-designed microkernel desktop could be on modest hardware.

BuaKzm7Kq9Q.summary: Marques Brownlee explains why iMessage's blue and green bubbles matter, covering the technical, commercial and social side of Apple's messaging lock-in. It also discusses RCS and what could be done about it.
BuaKzm7Kq9Q.why: HN commenters recommend it as an eloquent, well-rounded summary of the blue-versus-green bubble issue.

Bz2-49q6DOI.summary: David Mitchell's Soapbox rant on employers who demand passion and enthusiasm from workers, using satire to skewer fake workplace passion.
Bz2-49q6DOI.why: HN people share it as a funny and apt take whenever job postings or recruiters demand passion.

BE77h7dmoQU.summary: The official Kubernetes documentary, part 1, tells how a handful of Google engineers, inspired by Docker's success, built a container orchestrator. It covers the internal resistance to open source and the competition of the container orchestrator wars.
BE77h7dmoQU.why: Cited for the history of why containers and Kubernetes took off, though one thread critiqued the documentary itself.

BN-34JfUrHY.summary: The Primitive Technology channel shows the making of a stone axe (celt) using only primitive tools and materials, from shaping and polishing a basalt head to making the wooden handle and hafting it.
BN-34JfUrHY.why: HN people value its authenticity: no cuts, no cheating, and real tool use done entirely with materials found on site.

B8DjTcANBx0.summary: Craig Heffner's Black Hat 2013 talk on exploiting network surveillance cameras, covering how insecure their firmware is. It shows how easily such devices can be compromised.
B8DjTcANBx0.why: HN cites it as a fun and damning illustration of how poor security is in IP cameras, even expensive ones.

BJEHsvW2J6M.summary: LifebyMikeG lists 15 common mistakes beginner sourdough bakers make, with advice on fixing sticky, wet dough and other issues.
BJEHsvW2J6M.why: HN bakers point to it as a good video for learning the sourdough process.

BT5L4YU_Fl4.summary: An Empire Files episode giving a timeline of Zionist settlement, the Nakba and Israel's expansion over Palestinian land, presented from a critical, anti-colonial viewpoint. It previews Abby Martin's reporting in Palestine.
BT5L4YU_Fl4.why: HN commenters link it as a history of Palestine's colonization, though others dismiss it as propaganda.

BTURkjYJ_uk.summary: An excerpt from a Bay Area Rust meetup on Servo's WebRender, which renders CSS display lists on the GPU at very high frame rates. It explains the approach and demos rendering at around 500 FPS.
BTURkjYJ_uk.why: HN commenters point to it when discussing how WebRender works and as evidence of what GPU-based browser rendering can achieve.

Bch5B23_pu0.summary: Episode 7 of the Inside Koenigsegg series, where Christian von Koenigsegg demonstrates the camless Free Valve engine technology. It discusses how such innovation could affect the wider auto industry.
Bch5B23_pu0.why: Cited in threads on camless, digital valve and free-piston engines as a look at Koenigsegg's freevalve work.

BcyYyyaPz84.summary: ADVChina tours Chinese ghost cities and discusses the housing bubble, with speculative buyers purchasing empty apartments as investments.
BcyYyyaPz84.why: Linked in threads on China's property glut as visual evidence of empty, investment-driven housing, later seen as foreshadowing Evergrande.

BemHqUqcpI8.summary: A compilation of police interrogations of innocent suspects who behave in very different ways yet are treated as guilty. It illustrates how interrogation tactics and detectives' assumptions can distort the truth.
BemHqUqcpI8.why: HN commenters use it to show that behavior in interrogations is not a reliable sign of guilt and that police lie to innocent people.

Bf1GjCaYzYg.summary: IEEE Spectrum interviews Samsung display researcher Johan Feenstra on how electrowetting displays work. He explains why they can match LCD capability while being about three times more efficient.
Bf1GjCaYzYg.why: HN commenters bring it up as a look at a promising display technology that has stayed outside the mainstream.

Bm7L-2J52GU.summary: Technology Connections explains how an ordinary tank water heater works, including twin-element designs, and why it is cleverer than it looks.
Bm7L-2J52GU.why: Pointed to as a good, detailed explanation of how water heaters work and how to save power with them.

Bo3lUw9GUJA.summary: Dodoid gives an in-depth look at an SGI Onyx RealityEngine2, a $250,000 graphics supercomputer from 1993, covering its history, a physical overview, a teardown and some demos and games.
Bo3lUw9GUJA.why: Shared as a nostalgic tour of SGI hardware for people who remember that era.

Boi0XEm9-4E.summary: Streetfilms shows how Utrecht reduced car traffic in its center by removing roadways, building huge bike parking near the train station, and making cycling transitions safer and easier.
Boi0XEm9-4E.why: HN users cite it as a short, inspiring look at the Dutch approach to bike-friendly urban planning.

BpT6MkCeP7Y.summary: A short preview of OTOY's Brigade 3.0 engine doing real-time path tracing, running on two GTX Titans.
BpT6MkCeP7Y.why: HN cites it as the example of real-time GPU path tracing, noting its noise problem.

Bw-opH4f8Qg.summary: A Microsoft Flight Simulator Feature Discovery episode in which CEO Sebastian Wloch explains the new aerodynamics simulation for the 2020 release.
Bw-opH4f8Qg.why: HN commenters link it as official evidence that the new simulator's flight model is serious and comparable to dedicated sims.

Bx08yRsR9ow.summary: Yandex shows its self-driving taxi navigating snowy Moscow streets after a heavy snowfall, dealing with traffic, pedestrians, parked cars and snowbanks on real roads.
Bx08yRsR9ow.why: Cited as evidence that Yandex already runs capable self-driving cars in harsh weather, though some commenters doubted the footage.

BxV14h0kFs0.summary: Tom Scott's video whose title shows its own live view count, and the story of how he made that work. It explains why open APIs were once common and why they largely disappeared.
BxV14h0kFs0.why: The go-to citation for why free, open APIs get shut down and for the fate of services like Yahoo Pipes.

BzznBt8tVnI.summary: 12tone tells the story of pitch inflation and how concert A came to be standardized at 440 Hz, including attempts at legal standards. It is a short music history explainer.
BzznBt8tVnI.why: HN recommends it as an interesting explanation of how concert pitch ended up at exactly 440 Hz.

B2LLB9CGfLs.summary: The TruCoat scene from the Coen brothers' Fargo, in which car salesman Jerry Lundegaard sells an irate customer undercoating he never ordered.
B2LLB9CGfLs.why: Posted as a joke in threads about dealer add-on fees and subscription car features.

B3EBs7sCOzo.summary: A one-minute Grand Tour clip in which James May explains what happens if you drive a car in Germany without a licence.
B3EBs7sCOzo.why: Posted as a joke or 'reminds me of this' reply, not as a recommendation.

B6fnfVJzZT4.summary: A one-minute 2007 clip of Barack Obama, during his campaign, opposing warrantless wiretaps. It was later reposted with a campaign call to action.
B6fnfVJzZT4.why: HN uses it as a critical reference to contrast his campaign promises with later NSA surveillance policy.

B6rKUf9DWRI.summary: Highlights from Doug Engelbart's December 1968 demonstration at SRI, the first public showing of the mouse, hypertext, windows, real-time collaborative editing and shared-screen teleconferencing. This is a roughly six-minute condensed version of the full demo.
B6rKUf9DWRI.why: HN uses it as the go-to reference for how many modern computing ideas, collaboration included, were demonstrated in 1968.

B6vr1x6KDaY.summary: A TU Vienna demo of a double inverted pendulum on a cart, using constrained feedforward and optimal feedback control for swing-up and point-to-point motion.
B6vr1x6KDaY.why: Cited as a harder real-world version of the pole-balancing problem and as proof that chaotic systems can be controlled.

B7MIJP90biM.summary: A one-minute response video to the viral 'The Expert' sketch. It shows how to draw seven perpendicular red lines, some in green ink, some in transparent ink, one shaped like a kitten.
B7MIJP90biM.why: Posted as a joke whenever threads discuss impossible or contradictory specifications and clients, to show a clever solution exists.

B8C5sjjhsso.summary: A short montage from HBO's Silicon Valley of the TechCrunch Disrupt scene, in which founders repeat the phrase 'making the world a better place'.
B8C5sjjhsso.why: HN mostly cites it as a joke or parody whenever startups or tech companies claim lofty missions.

B8R148hFxPw.summary: Waymo's 2018 360-degree video lets viewers look around inside a fully driverless ride. It is built from footage and real-time data of an actual trip on city streets.
B8R148hFxPw.why: Cited as a reference in self-driving threads for what the car senses, such as sensor range, LIDAR and planning, although some commenters were critical of it.

B9MShtCg4fk.summary: A complete rendition of John Williams' Imperial March rearranged in a major key. The change turns Vader's menacing theme into something triumphant.
B9MShtCg4fk.why: Used as a counter-example in music theory discussions to show how mode changes a melody's mood.

B9tzoGFszog.summary: A Yes Minister sketch in which Jim Hacker and Sir Humphrey meet the BBC and discuss its independence from government pressure. It is a satirical look at the relationship between the state and the broadcaster.
B9tzoGFszog.why: HN quotes it jokingly whenever the BBC or government control of media is in the news.

BGGOn-H7s3Q.summary: A sketch from The Peter Serafinowicz Show parodying Apple product launches with the absurdly tiny 'Mactini'.
BGGOn-H7s3Q.why: Used as a joke when Apple products get smaller or more minimal.

BGPGknpq3e0.summary: A short BBC clip narrated by David Attenborough showing crows in Japan using city traffic to crack nuts, dropping them at intersections and retrieving them when the light changes.
BGPGknpq3e0.why: HN uses it as the standard illustration of animal tool use and adaptive intelligence in crow threads.

BGrfhsxxmdE.summary: A one-minute Simpsons clip from the Homerpalooza episode, featuring the song 'It'll Happen to You'.
BGrfhsxxmdE.why: Only posted as a joke reply about getting old or out of touch.

BHup81lEjqo.summary: A short clip of Venetian Snares' track 'Look' from Songs About My Cats (2001), shown as a spectrogram. The audio encodes an image in its frequency content.
BHup81lEjqo.why: Cited as an example of artists hiding visuals in audio spectrograms.

BKKg4lZ_o-Y.summary: Scott Manley's short animation shows every asteroid discovery from 1970 to 2015 plotted over time in 8K. It makes visible how survey technology made discoveries accelerate and where telescopes looked.
BKKg4lZ_o-Y.why: HN uses it as a quick visual reference for how asteroid detection capability grew and how discovery patterns are biased by survey geometry.

BKm8FolQ7jw.summary: A short National Geographic piece showing a laser system that tracks and kills mosquitoes, filmed in slow motion, as part of anti-malaria efforts. It comes from Intellectual Ventures' 2010 work.
BKm8FolQ7jw.why: HN commenters bring it up as proof that laser mosquito defense is technically feasible, in threads about DIY pest-zapping projects.

BKorP55Aqvg.summary: A comedy sketch of a business meeting in which an engineer, the expert, is asked to do impossible things like draw red lines with blue ink.
BKorP55Aqvg.why: Shared constantly as a painfully accurate depiction of absurd requirements, clueless management and estimation pressure.

BRqZBuu_Ers.summary: Oh The Urbanity! tests the theory that banning housing investors would fix affordability, using Rotterdam's ban as a case study. The video finds mixed results.
BRqZBuu_Ers.why: Cited as a real-world experiment showing that banning investors did not lower purchase prices and may have raised rents.

BV32Cs_CMqo.summary: Mozilla's short demo of Unreal Engine 3 running in Firefox, ported by Mozilla and Epic in four days using Emscripten and asm.js.
BV32Cs_CMqo.why: HN cites it as proof of how capable browsers became, a landmark for asm.js and WebAssembly.

BYVZh5kqaFg.summary: Mark Rober and Joe Barnard drop an egg from a high-altitude balloon, using a camera-guided glider to steer it to a safe landing.
BYVZh5kqaFg.why: Used as an example of how easy homing and guidance have become, resembling precision-guided munitions.

BZoKfap4g4w.summary: Hans Rosling makes the case that the washing machine was the greatest invention of the industrial revolution. Using Gapminder graphics, he shows how electricity and economic growth free up time for reading and learning.
BZoKfap4g4w.why: Referenced when discussing how much time household technology saved families and how heavy housework used to be.

Bd0cMmBvqWc.summary: A campaign-produced compilation of clips of Donald Trump condemning racism and white supremacy on 38 occasions, published in 2020.
Bd0cMmBvqWc.why: Linked in election-era threads as evidence in arguments over whether Trump disavowed white supremacist groups.

Bg3RAI8uyVw.summary: A game-dev video demonstrating a noise shader in Godot where shapes are visible only in motion against animated noise and vanish when the game is paused or screenshotted. The demo is available on GitHub.
Bg3RAI8uyVw.why: HN people cite it as the origin of the vanishing-in-a-screenshot effect, used in ideas for captchas and AI-resistant text.

BhMSzC1crr0.summary: SpaceX's official footage of the CRS-6 Falcon 9 first stage landing attempt, in high resolution and slow motion. It shows the descent and touchdown on the drone ship.
BhMSzC1crr0.why: HN uses it as a reference clip for examining landing behavior such as engine gimballing, and comparing against failed early landings.

Bmz67ErIRa4.summary: A short clip from the 1995 film Hackers in which the characters attempt to hack the Gibson supercomputer, shown with flashy stylized visuals of digital intrusion.
Bmz67ErIRa4.why: Used mostly as a punchline or example of cheesy, unrealistic Hollywood depictions of hacking and over-stylized tech UIs.

Bu1YFshFuI4.summary: Archival 1978 Sandia footage testing shipping containers for spent nuclear fuel, including trucks ramming walls, a locomotive hitting a truck-borne cask and a rocket-propelled train crash, plus a fire test.
Bu1YFshFuI4.why: Cited in nuclear power threads as proof that waste casks survive severe crashes.

BwoiFC-HwPE.summary: Drone footage over Tesla's Fremont factory in January 2021 that captures a Gigapress die-casting machine in operation.
